newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians jailed and fined for anti-govt protest.
newsitem.headline: Albanians jailed and fined for anti-govt protest.

text.p: Some 52 Albanians who took part in a demonstration last Sunday in Tirana's Skanderbeg Square have been jailed or given hefty fines on charges of joining an illegal protest, court officials said on Wednesday.

Tirana district court's chief judge Qazim Gjonaj said 13 out of 54 defendants had been sentenced to between one and two weeks in jail for participating in an illegal protest. The others were fined 5,000 to 20,000 leks (about $50-200). Two were acquitted.

"After five trials, sentences were handed out to those detained last Sunday after an illegal gathering in defiance of a warning. Such actions are punishable with up to three months imprisonment according to the penal code," Gjonaj told Reuters.
The fines could wipe out more than a month's wages for some defendants with the average Albanian monthly salary at around 8,000 leks ($73).

The opposition Socialist newspaper Zeri i Popullit said the state had started proceedings against opposition leaders who led the protest. In response, the party would attempt to sue the state for using violence during the demonstration, it added.

Thousands of people staged demonstrations in Tirana and other major cities last week, blaming President Sali Berisha's right-wing government for the loss of their savings through the collapse of widespread pyramid investment schemes.
The government on Tuesday announced it had set up a commission to investigate the get-rich-quick schemes that have ruined thousands.
"I lost 500,000 leks in one (scheme) and 30,000 in another," a desperate Tirana policeman said on Wednesday. "Now I should support my family with my monthly salary of 8,000 leks. Is it possible?"
The government said it would initiate legislation in parliament next week to bring a halt to pyramid-style borrowing schemes in Europe's poorest country.
Last week it ordered the seizure of 25.5 billion leks ($255 million) deposited by such schemes in state-owned banks.
Reports in the Albanian press said the managers of the Gjallica company and the Xhaferri foundation, two of the most popular pyramid schemes in the country, had been arrested.

The Socialists have called for peaceful protests over the next two days in the western city of Durres and in Tirana "in continuing support for popular protests because of the deepening (pyramid) scheme crisis".
The Greek ambassador to Albania Costantinos Prevedurakis said he feared the collapse of the schemes could spark another wave of Albanian emigration to his country.

"I am afraid we shall have a second wave of immigration and it will happen at the moment when we are trying to stabilise the first wave of immigrants by applying an agreement on seasonal labour," he told Reuters.
Pyramid schemes burgeoned in Albania after the fall of communism in 1990, luring thousands of Albanians into selling their homes, land and livestock with promises of big returns.
But three of them have crumbled so far, leaving thousands out of pocket. Four more have suspended payments to investors.
